title: OAN Discovery — Request Troubleshooting
description: One transaction, end to end. Reached from the Service Overview's failed-requests table.

options.content:
Paste a **transaction ID** or a **trace ID** above, or arrive here by clicking either column in **Recent failed requests** on the Service Overview. Both boxes work; fill in one.

Both exist because an envelope-rejected request has no `beckn.transactionId` at all — the context never parsed, which is what it was rejected for. Those requests are findable only by trace ID.

Spans and logs join on `beckn.transactionId` / `transaction_id` — not on trace context. beckn-onix extracts `traceparent` inbound and injects it on no outbound call, so each participant's span roots its own trace and a waterfall across participants is not available. This table is the honest substitute.

panels.title: Trace waterfall
panels.description: The native trace view. Expand a span to read its attributes, and the span events nested inside it -- request_info, retrieval_info, response_info and error.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  "TraceId" AS traceID,
  "SpanId" AS spanID,
  "ParentSpanId" AS parentSpanID,
  "ServiceName" AS serviceName,
  "SpanName" AS operationName,
  multiply(toUnixTimestamp64Nano("Timestamp"), 0.000001) AS startTime,
  -- Duration is nanoseconds in this schema. Get the factor wrong and the
  -- waterfall renders at the wrong scale with nothing to indicate it.
  multiply("Duration", 0.000001) AS duration,
  arrayMap(key -> map('key', key, 'value', "SpanAttributes"[key]), mapKeys("SpanAttributes")) AS tags,
  arrayMap(key -> map('key', key, 'value', "ResourceAttributes"[key]), mapKeys("ResourceAttributes")) AS serviceTags,
  if("StatusCode" IN ('Error', 'STATUS_CODE_ERROR'), 2, 0) AS statusCode,
  -- Span events become the expandable entries inside the span. This is
  -- where request_info / retrieval_info / response_info / error live, and
  -- on this service that is most of the content worth reading.
  arrayMap((name, timestamp, attributes) -> tuple(name, toString(toUnixTimestamp64Milli(timestamp)),
    arrayMap(key -> map('key', key, 'value', attributes[key]), mapKeys(attributes)))
    ::Tuple(name String, timestamp String, fields Array(Map(String, String))),
    "Events".Name, "Events".Timestamp, "Events".Attributes) AS logs,
  "SpanKind" AS kind
FROM "otel"."otel_traces"
-- Accepts either entry point: a trace id straight from the link, or a
-- transaction id typed in, resolved to its trace here.
WHERE traceID = if('$trace_id' != '', '$trace_id',
  (SELECT "TraceId" FROM "otel"."otel_traces"
   WHERE "SpanAttributes"['beckn.transactionId'] = '$transaction_id' LIMIT 1))

panels.title: Spans for this transaction
panels.description: Every span carrying this transaction id, in order. With only discovery-service instrumented today this is usually one row; it becomes a per-hop breakdown once the adapters emit.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  Timestamp AS time,
  ServiceName AS service,
  SpanName AS span,
  round(Duration / 1e6, 2) AS duration_ms,
  SpanAttributes['http.status_code'] AS http_status,
  SpanAttributes['result.empty'] AS empty_result,
  SpanAttributes['beckn.messageId'] AS message_id,
  TraceId,
  SpanId
FROM otel.otel_traces
WHERE $__timeFilter(Timestamp)
  AND (
    ('$transaction_id' != '' AND SpanAttributes['beckn.transactionId'] = '$transaction_id')
    OR ('$trace_id' != '' AND TraceId = '$trace_id')
  )
ORDER BY Timestamp

panels.title: Span events
panels.description: request_info, retrieval_info, response_info and error, flattened. This is where the intent shape, the providers that answered and the error cause live -- none of them are span attributes.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  ev.1 AS event,
  arrayStringConcat(
    arrayMap(k -> concat(k, ' = ', ev.2[k]), arraySort(mapKeys(ev.2))), '\n'
  ) AS attributes
FROM otel.otel_traces
ARRAY JOIN arrayZip(Events.Name, Events.Attributes) AS ev
WHERE $__timeFilter(Timestamp)
  AND (
    ('$transaction_id' != '' AND SpanAttributes['beckn.transactionId'] = '$transaction_id')
    OR ('$trace_id' != '' AND TraceId = '$trace_id')
  )
ORDER BY event

panels.title: Log lines for this transaction
panels.description: Joined on the ids the collector's transform/logs stage lifts out of the zap JSON body -- NOT on the otel_logs.TraceId column, which is empty for every filelog-sourced line in this stack.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  Timestamp AS timestamp,
  Body AS body,
  SeverityText AS level,
  ServiceName
FROM otel.otel_logs
WHERE $__timeFilter(Timestamp)
  AND (
    ('$transaction_id' != '' AND LogAttributes['transaction_id'] = '$transaction_id')
    -- LogAttributes, not the TraceId column: these logs arrive through the
    -- filelog receiver reading container stdout, so the collector never
    -- populates the native column -- the id is a field inside the zap JSON
    -- that transform/logs parsed out. The column is empty on 11600 of
    -- 11601 rows. TraceId is kept as an OR for anything delivered by OTLP.
    OR ('$trace_id' != '' AND (LogAttributes['trace_id'] = '$trace_id' OR TraceId = '$trace_id'))
  )
ORDER BY Timestamp DESC
LIMIT 200
